clue.text: Such blow-outs should lack point for an ascetic

definitions.text: Such blow-outs should lack point for an ascetic

parts.words: Such blow-outs should lack point for an ascetic
parts.note: blow-outs are lavish meals; take away a compass point (E for east) and the word left is the abstinence an ascetic practises

explanation.surface: A warning that big blow-outs are pointless for someone living a life of self-denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' is a compass point, E, whose removal turns the word for blow-outs into FASTS, the ascetic's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Blow-outs are big celebratory meals, slang for banquets.

clue.text: Remove traces of a seer

indicators.note: read as re-move, to move again, so the letters of the following words are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to wipe out every sign that a prophet was ever present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remove' does double service as the whole clue's sense and, read as 're-move', the signal to rearrange A SEER.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub out or obliterate all signs of something is to expunge it.

clue.text: Ships with cargoes of sherry?

parts.note: two-masted sailing vessels share their name with the tall glasses sherry is served in, so these vessels hold sherry

explanation.definitionFit: The sailing vessels are fore-and-aft rigged craft, and the same word names large sherry glasses.

clue.text: Keeps short birds

explanation.surface: A note about someone rationing food for small birds.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep someone short is to be sparing with supplies; the birds are small sandpipers of that name.

clue.text: A monster, whether a fairy in a dream or not

parts.note: the old construction 'be he X or not' means 'whether he is X or not', so whether ... or not gives these words
Moth is one of Titania's fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: Describing a monster that may or may not be some dream fairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whether ... or not' is the inverted 'be he Moth or not'; the 'or not' completes that idiom and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical beast in Job has become the general word for any huge monstrous creature.

clue.text: Rest and refreshment but no pension

definitions.text: Rest and refreshment but no pension

parts.words: Rest and refreshment but no pension
parts.note: a night's lodging and a morning meal, but not the full board a continental pension offers

explanation.definitionFit: Lodging for the night plus a morning meal is the guest-house arrangement short of full board.

clue.text: "O, ——! O, ——! most ——!" (Hamlet)

parts.note: the Ghost's cry in Hamlet, Act 1 Scene 5, with the same dreadful adjective filling each blank

explanation.definitionFit: The Ghost of Hamlet's father uses this word for his own murder, meaning dreadful or appalling.

clue.text: Claret with some steamed octopus !

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dinner order: red wine to go with a plate of steamed octopus.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux, and this Bordeaux district makes it.

clue.text: A temporary switch for Eve, perhaps

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker, so the shortening stands for temporary
a switch is a hank of hair, as is a tress

explanation.surface: Eve might be hired as a stopgap office worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' looks like a change of jobs but is a lock of hair; Eve tempted Adam, hence the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve enticed Adam to eat the apple, the first seductress, a woman who lures.

clue.text: Fenimore Cooper pioneer dropping marker flares

explanation.surface: An American frontiersman somehow flying a bombing raid.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty Bumppo is the scout of James Fenimore Cooper's novel of that title; RAF target-marking aircraft in the war bore the same name.

clue.text: Cheat me at St. Peter's

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or swindle them

explanation.surface: A complaint about being swindled in Rome's great basilica.
explanation.definitionFit: St Peter's Basilica in Rome is famous for Michelangelo's vast cupola, the feature named here.

clue.text: Born to be the father of a decade ?

parts.note: to father a child is to beget it; the past form is begot
a decade is a period of ten years, so it gives ten

explanation.surface: Wondering whether someone was born to sire ten children.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought into being by a parent, as in 'only begotten Son', means born.

clue.text: Urge on visibly if audibly

indicators.note: audibly says the words for visibly are to be heard, not read, giving their spoken twin

parts.note: something visible is in sight, so the clue word gives that phrase

explanation.surface: Encourage someone, whether they can be seen or heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur or goad someone into action is to stir them up.

clue.text: Head may have this problem

parts.note: add this pain to the word head and you get a common complaint of the skull

explanation.definitionFit: A dull continuous pain is the problem; head plus it makes the familiar complaint.

clue.text: Anger a cat from Port of Spain

indicators.note: the port is made from the letters of the preceding words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A cat's fury in Port of Spain, the capital of Trinidad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port of Spain' looks like the Trinidad capital but means a port in Spain; 'from' signals the anagram of ANGER A CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: This Mediterranean naval port lies in Murcia, south-east Spain.

clue.text: Is there no more gin in Derbyshire ?

parts.note: Bols is a Dutch distiller known for its genever, Dutch gin
something no more is over, finished

explanation.surface: A drinker in Derbyshire asking whether the gin has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'Bols over?', the question 'Is there no more gin?'. Derbyshire is an English county; the answer is a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town in north-east Derbyshire with a hilltop castle, a place found in that county.

clue.text: Transplant arranger?

parts.note: read as one who deals in body parts, a surgeon who arranges to move hearts and kidneys

explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who arranges things is a planner or coordinator; the pun splits the word to mean one who handles body parts.

clue.text: Fatherly friend swallows a tear

indicators.note: swallows means the word for friend takes the other pieces into its middle

parts.note: pal is an informal word for a friend
a rent is a rip or tear in cloth

explanation.surface: A kindly father figure gulping down a tear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' reads as weeping but is a rip, RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the qualities of a father or mother is relating to a parent.

clue.text: Training in obedience after the fall

definitions.text: Training in obedience after the fall

parts.words: Training in obedience after the fall
parts.note: horse training in obedience, read also as the era of clothing that began after Adam and Eve's fall

explanation.definitionFit: The equestrian art of training a horse in precise obedient movements; split, it reads as the age of clothes after Eden.

clue.text: Death is imminent at the last

definitions.text: Death is imminent at the last

parts.words: Death is imminent at the last
parts.note: the idiom 'at the last' plus this word means at the point of dying, the final breath

explanation.definitionFit: A sudden sharp intake of breath; the final one is the dying breath of the idiom.

clue.text: Neutral gear

parts.note: clothing made for either men or women, rather than the car gear with no drive

explanation.definitionFit: Clothing designed for both men and women is gender-neutral in style.

clue.text: Faded out of father's diocese ?

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, with the possessive
a bishop's see is his diocese

explanation.surface: Something that has faded and fallen out of favour in Dad's bishopric.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman or style past her prime, out of fashion, is past it.

clue.text: Make a bow from the platform

explanation.surface: Taking a bow from the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To bend down is to bow the body; in American use it is also a raised porch or platform at a house door.

clue.text: Benevolence of a sort shown by the Head

parts.note: a kind is a sort or type
ness is a headland, a promontory, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A headmaster displaying a certain kind of goodwill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Head' looks like a headmaster but is a headland, NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Benevolence and friendly generosity are the quality of being good-natured.

clue.text: A balk in a wheel

parts.note: the idiom of putting a rod in someone's wheel, to obstruct their plans

explanation.definitionFit: A rod from hub to rim; 'to put one in someone's wheel' is to thwart them, a balk or hindrance.

clue.text: Hour of the balloon's ascent

parts.note: the launch time of an operation, when the balloon goes up, meaning the action starts

explanation.definitionFit: The appointed start time of an operation is 'nought' hour; 'the balloon goes up' is the idiom for things starting.

clue.text: There are sound reasons for valve replacement

definitions.text: There are sound reasons for valve replacement

parts.words: There are sound reasons for valve replacement
parts.note: radios, which deal in sound, changed from glass valves to solid-state devices

explanation.definitionFit: The solid-state device replaced the thermionic valve (vacuum tube) in radio sets.

clue.text: Paperback Dad allowed at inside rate

indicators.note: inside says the speed abbreviation is set within the other words' letters

parts.note: pa is an informal word for Dad
let means allowed or permitted
mph, miles per hour, is a rate of speed

explanation.surface: Dad lets his paperback go at the cheap indoor rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A small booklet with paper covers, a softbound publication.

clue.text: One sent back (as sex king?) to Persia

indicators.note: sent back means the whole run of letters is read from end to start

parts.note: taken as written
rex is Latin for king, as in the royal signature

explanation.surface: A man returned to Persia, perhaps as a sex king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent back' reverses SEX + REX; 'to Persia' places the man, the Persian king who invaded Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A single person, here a king of ancient Persia, son of Darius.
